messages:
ravi: hey team, ravi here. first-day CI attempt hitting a weird failure: Buildkite job bootstraps then the agent logs show 'unauthorized: invalid token'. I tried creating a PAT and adding it to pipeline vars but still blocked. anyone seen SSO/pat weirdness during onboarding?

claire: welcome! :wave: GitHub org enforces SAML SSO — PATs created before you authorize SSO are blocked for org access until you explicitly authorize them. Did you click the 'Authorize' button on the org SSO page after creating the PAT?

ravi: ah i created the PAT then immediately set CI_GH_PAT in Buildkite. how do i authorize SSO? i don't see the button in the UI.

juan: if you go to https://github.com/organizations/redwood/settings/sso (or the org home page) there should be an "Authorize this token for use with your organization" dialog after you create the PAT. sometimes it only shows up after you sign in with SSO. also check your email for a SAML confirmation.

ravi: here's the Buildkite snippet from the agent: 
```
2026-03-22T15:02:10Z agent: registering
2026-03-22T15:02:11Z agent: POST https://api.github.com/orgs/redwood/packages/lookup 403
{"message":"SAML authorization required for personal access token"}
```

emily: yep that error is the tell. Two paths: 1) authorize the PAT via org SSO (recommended), or 2) get added to the redwood-ci Okta group so we can inject the org app token for your pipeline runs. which do you prefer for now?

ravi: prefer to authorize my PAT so it's reproducible. where's the UI?

claire: go to your account > Applications > Authorized OAuth Apps (or directly to the org SSO page). There should be a banner prompting SAML authorization for tokens. If it's not appearing, try sign-out and sign-in with SSO (use the 'Sign in with SAML' button).

ravi: did SSO sign-in and then authorized the token. restarted the Buildkite job but still seeing unauthorized. build link: https://buildkite.com/redwood/infra-pipeline/builds/789

juan: two more gotchas: a) Buildkite caches pipeline vars, you might need to restart the build to pick up new masked vars (you did) and b) the PAT scope must include repo or packages depending on what the job calls. what scopes does your PAT have?

ravi: scopes: repo (public_repo), read:packages. created as expiring 24h token.

emily: looks good. infra-bot, can you check whether the pipeline's masked var CI_GH_PAT is present for ravi's pipeline?

infra-bot: Masked env var CI_GH_PAT present on pipeline infra-pipeline for user ravi. Access request CI-20011 created for audit.

ravi: re-run again...

ravi:  build now fails earlier with agent version mismatch: "agent version 4.2.0 not compatible with server 4.3.1". did we have a pinned runner image?

claire: ah that explains it — our runner image used by the pipeline was recently bumped and some hosts still had an older agent cached. we recently added a post in onboarding about clearing local Buildkite agent caches / pulling latest runner image. try deleting the local image or set the Buildkite step to pull: always.

ravi: pulled latest image locally and restarted the job  this time the agent registered and the build proceeded :tada: tests running. thanks everyone!!

juan: welcome aboard, and adding a quick checklist note: "If PAT blocked, authorize SAML SSO; ensure PAT has repo/read:packages scopes; if agent 'unauthorized' switches to 'version mismatch', pull latest runner image or set pull: always."

emily: i'll add that to the onboarding doc and drop a one-liner in the new hire checklist. :memo: welcome again!"
